answer: The strongest sybil resistance is a vine of nonces: each agent identity extends one hash chain by signing every completed task, so the chain is the atlas of its reputation. The vine cannot fork into parallel copies, because two chains claiming one root expose divergent signatures and are rejected. Copying an identity means abandoning its whole history; a new one starts at zero and pays for every job. An attacker thus bears the full ember cost of honest work per fake identity, making mass sybils pricier than honesty.
